correctness.rationale: Global addition of any H=F2² colour preserves properness, so every nonbalanced frequency cancels. For balanced frequencies, choose one root colour zero and divide the orbit sum by four. The S3 permutation of nonzero colour names acts on root-fixed proper colourings and makes each nonzero colour equinumerous at each other vertex. Each binary coordinate equals one at precisely two of three such colours, so the sum of every coordinate bit over root-fixed colourings is even. Therefore the number of negative phases is even, W/4≡P_G(4)/4 (mod4). The linear chromatic coefficient a1 determines the parity of P_G(4)/4. For K_m,n with m,n≥2 the Stirling expansion P/4≡3^n+2S(m,3)≡(-1)^(m+n) (mod4), proving exact full balanced support and rank. This covers disconnected/empty colouring cases within the stated nonempty graph scope.

value.rationale: Proper-colouring Fourier support is a natural exact counting-convolution and recovery invariant. The result links a standard chromatic coefficient to *every* balanced high-degree character and proves exact deconvolution rank for arbitrary-size complete bipartite graphs, not just a numerical biclique. Mod16 divisibility is nontrivial beyond forced global-translation zeros; the odd-a1 hypothesis exposes a meaningful structural sufficient condition.

limitations: The odd chromatic linear coefficient is sufficient rather than necessary.
Does not determine minimum positive multiplier magnitude exactly beyond lower bound four or full magnitude distribution.
Only Klein-four colour group, not arbitrary four-colour cyclic group or other group.
